title: Branching space-time
exact_version: DOI 10.1007/BF00414289 (Crossref-verified); JSTOR scan of the Synthese printing, read 2026-10-28 via the exa cache of the now-dead mirror https://homepages.uc.edu/~martinj/History_of_Logic/Aristotle/De_interpretatione/Belnap%20--%20Branching%20Space-Time.pdf (live URL returns 404; scan header confirms 'Synthese, Vol. 92, No. 3 (Sep., 1992), pp. 385-434')
section_locator: Def. 7 (compatibility) p. 394; substantive commitments (1)-(3) p. 395 (horizon caveat); Def. 11 (space-like separated = causal contemporaries) and Fact 12 p. 397; Postulate 13 (historical connection) p. 398; 'wings' problem posed p. 400; Postulate 28 (Prior Choice Principle, point event version) p. 409; Sec. 8 'The problem of the wings' with Facts 30-31 pp. 410-412
relevance: Founding BST paper. Sets the modal (history-based) notion of what is settled/real at a point event; states the common-causal-future (upward directedness) requirement; explicitly flags event horizons as threatening it (X1 ingredient); solves the wings problem modally, not causally (X3 ingredient).
limits: JSTOR scan OCR is noisy; quotations below are marked where word order was repaired. Paywalled at JSTOR; page numbers taken from the scan's printed headers.
assumptions: Our World as a set of possible point events with a causal partial order; no backward branching; Prior Choice Principle; histories are maximal upward-directed (common causal future) subsets
conclusion: BST92 defines compatibility via common causal future; horizon cases tabled as physical questions; elsewhere ('wing') events belong to the intersection of the histories through a choice point
proof_status: Authors' proofs in paper; Facts 30-31 are proved by stipulated model analysis, not read line-by-line here
open_questions: Whether any later BST work picked up the tabled horizon question (none found in the sources read)

Ringström 2009 p. 188 quote; 9.3.5 global vs local determinism pp. 329-333; 9.3.7 summary pp. 338-339; ch. 10.5 causae causantes dynamic time p. 362
relevance: The authoritative BST monograph. Whole-book keyword scan (all 456 pages): 'horizon' 0 hits, 'de Sitter' 0 hits, 'causal potential' 0 hits, 'growth' 0 hits, 'MGHD' 0 hits, 'black hole' 0 hits, 'Correia' 0 hits, 'Rosenkranz' 0 hits, 'bow' 0 hits; 'settled' 38 hits (all modal/history-based usage); 'globally hyperbolic' 23 hits (ch. 9 IVP/determinism). title: Pruning Some Branches from "Branching Spacetimes"
venue: In D. Dieks (ed.), The Ontology of Spacetime II, Philosophy and Foundations of Physics vol. 4, Elsevier, ch. 10, pp. 187-205
exact_version: DOI 10.1016/S1871-1774(08)00010-7 (Crossref-verified); author's copy on his Pitt page (19 PDF pages = printed pp. 187-205)
section_locator: Sec. 2 (three types of branching) pp. 187-192; growing-block remark p. 191; footnote 12 (choice points and future null cones) p. 192; Sec. 3.2 no-go results pp. 193-195; Sec. 3.4 shortcomings of the non-Hausdorff option pp. 199-201; IVP determinism p. 201
relevance: The named critique of BST branching. Contains no horizons, no causal-potential realm, no de Sitter, and no influence-based settledness; its closest statements are footnote 12 (indeterministic influence radiating along/within future null cones of choice points) and the p. 201 IVP determinism remark (X4 premise).
limits: Author PDF verified page-accurate against printed headers.
conclusion: Individual branching is neither necessary nor sufficient for indeterminism; only the non-Hausdorff escape survives, at high cost; ensemble branching is the sense relevant to physics
proof_status: Tipler 1977 and Geroch 1967a results quoted, not re-derived

title: Indeterminism is a modal notion: branching spacetimes and Earman's pruning
exact_version: DOI 10.1007/s11229-010-9846-8 (Crossref-verified); read in the PhilSci-Archive preprint versioned 2011-02-01 (preprint pagination pp. 1-41; published pagination not checked)
section_locator: Sec. 2.1 (Our World and point events) preprint p. 8, '(settled) causal past' phrase; Sec. 2.4 space-like relatedness p. 10; Sec. 4.4 past/future asymmetry p. 35; Sec. 6 Final, 'An open task looms large' p. 40; whole-text keyword check: 'horizon' 0 hits
relevance: The BST school's reply to Earman 2008. Defines settled past via the causal order, treats OW as modally thick, and ends by declaring GR integration (which would include horizons) an open task. No common-future growth claims, no causal-potential realm, no horizons.
limits: Preprint pagination used; published version not fetched (paywalled).
conclusion: Ensemble-branching analyses of determinism (Montague-Lewis-Earman) and BST's modal indeterminism are distinct; MBS histories are isomorphic to Minkowski spacetime; GR-like BST models remain to be constructed
open_questions: GR-BST models (declared open in 2012; ch. 9 of BMP 2022 still cautious)

title: Defining determinism
venue: British Journal for the Philosophy of Science 69(1): 215-252
exact_version: DOI 10.1093/bjps/axv049 (Crossref/UCHicago-verified), open access CC BY-NC; read in the PhilSci accepted-version preprint (no page-accurate extraction; section heading '4 Branching-styl[e] ...' visible in text)
section_locator: Abstract and Sec. 4 (branching-based definition, DBRN): indeterminism iff 'some initial segment of its evolution can be continued in more than one alternative way'; Sec. 5-6 area, GR discussion: globally hyperbolic spacetimes, Cauchy surfaces, Choquet-Bruhat and Geroch [1969] maximal vacuum Cauchy development uniqueness quoted; whole-text keyword check: 'horizon' 0 hits, 'de Sitter' 0 hits, 'settled' 0 hits
relevance: Defines determinism/indeterminism for theories via branching models and maps the GR initial-value problem onto it. Anchors the determinism premise our X4 uses (agreement regions are temporal initial segments / Cauchy data), but contains no claim that a proper sub-slice causal realm fixes the future, and no horizons.
limits: Preprint text via exa extraction; exact section/page of the GR discussion not pinned.
conclusion: Branching-based definition combines clarity and philosophical content better than mapping- or equations-based definitions

title: Branching for general relativists
venue: In T. Müller (ed.), Nuel Belnap on Indeterminism and Free Action, Springer (Outstanding Contributions to Logic)
exact_version: Read in the PhilSci-Archive preprint (2013), file 'tomasz-placek-BST-for-GR-Pittarchive.pdf'; published 2014 volume page range not verified; footnote 2 of BMP 2022 cites it as Placek (2014)
section_locator: Sec. 1 Introduction, preprint p. 3: BST92 historicity criterion 'flies in the face of' Schwarzschild spacetime and the de Sitter cosmological model; 'later witness' condition x <= z, y <= z; whole-text keyword check: 'horizon' 0 hits
relevance: Closest BST-side statement of the X1 ingredient under a name: de Sitter (and Schwarzschild) fail the pairwise-common-future (maximal upward-directedness) criterion for belonging to one BST history, so the criterion is generalized. No existence-domain growth axiom (P1R), no horizons, no causal-potential realm.
conclusion: BST1992 must be generalized (choice pairs, generalized manifolds) to accommodate GR spacetimes lacking common futures
open_questions: Relation between the generalized historicity criterion and existence-domain growth (not discussed in the paper)
